method: Design FMEA: Severity/Occurrence/Detection each scored 1..10; RPN = S*O*D. Scores are engineering estimates and must be revised from field/runtime evidence.

review_policy.cadence: review on every architecture milestone, after any tunnel/routing incident, and before every release tag
review_policy.release_rule: no unresolved risk at or above the high-RPN threshold or critical-severity threshold; explicit accepted risks require acceptance_reason

risks.title: Partial Agent Tunnel startup leaves stale route/policy state
risks.failure_mode: sing-box changes part of TUN/routing state and startup then fails
risks.effect: host connectivity degradation or traffic routed differently after AntigravitiProxi reports failure
risks.cause: multi-step privileged OS networking mutation
controls: SIGKILL recovery test preserving unrelated route/rule state
risks.mitigation: complete crash-phase fault injection for every startup/journal boundary and keep recovery ownership-conservative
risks.verification: fault-injection tests fail each startup phase and prove owned TUN/route/rule state is removed while unrelated host state survives

risks.title: Antigravity helper is not attributed and bypasses selected VPN
risks.failure_mode: new or renamed IDE helper does not match process_name/process_path rules or cannot be tied to a live routed connection
risks.effect: agent generation uses an unintended egress and can fail geo/eligibility checks
risks.cause: Antigravity is multi-process and helper topology can change between IDE releases
controls: Windows exact source-endpoint to PID correlation
risks.mitigation: add full Windows Agent Tunnel PID/socket/outbound/external-egress proof and reviewed policy learning for newly discovered helpers
risks.verification: every active discovered helper PID is exactly attributed to a live socket and vpn-direct connection; unknown or ambiguous ownership prevents verified assurance

risks.title: Domain fallback captures unrelated Google traffic
risks.failure_mode: domain-only fallback sends unrelated processes contacting googleapis.com through vpn-direct
risks.effect: process-isolation invariant is weakened and unrelated applications can change network path
risks.cause: fallback is intentionally broader than process matching to catch unknown helpers
risks.mitigation: replace broad domain fallback with learned PID/path plus narrowly scoped endpoint policy while retaining explicit isolation-relaxed state
risks.verification: negative integration tests prove non-Antigravity Google clients retain system-direct in strict mode and relaxed mode is explicit when enabled

risks.title: VPN interface recreation invalidates bind_interface
risks.failure_mode: VPN reconnect creates a new interface/index or makes the configured interface temporarily unavailable
risks.effect: Agent Tunnel stops working or remains degraded until reconfigured
risks.cause: desktop VPN clients frequently recreate TUN/WireGuard interfaces
controls: preflight checks selected interface exists and is UP
external-egress assurance cannot become verified without observable vpn-direct path
risks.mitigation: watch interface lifecycle and re-resolve/rebind selected VPN using stable identity plus route probes
risks.verification: integration test disconnects/recreates VPN interface and proves automatic degraded-to-healthy recovery

risks.title: IPv6 or DNS path leaks outside intended egress
risks.failure_mode: IPv4 follows vpn-direct while IPv6 or resolver traffic follows another path
risks.effect: inconsistent geolocation, DNS poisoning exposure or backend failure
risks.cause: dual-stack OS routing and resolver behavior differ across platforms/distributions
controls: DNS fingerprint persisted as recovery evidence
public-egress parser accepts IPv4/IPv6 but production assurance is not yet family-independent
risks.mitigation: separate IPv4/IPv6 health and egress verification; explicitly test DNS and UDP/QUIC paths
risks.verification: dual-stack integration matrix proves A/AAAA DNS and TCP/UDP/QUIC egress use the selected policy
plan_refs: P2/P4 IPv4/IPv6 DNS UDP QUIC assurance

risks.title: Privileged networking and desktop control plane are insufficiently separated
risks.failure_mode: whole application is elevated to obtain TUN privileges
risks.effect: larger privileged attack surface and risk of root/admin-owned desktop state
risks.cause: platform TUN operations need privilege and Windows minimal-helper separation is not complete
controls: managed sing-box path/symlink/owner/SHA-256 revalidation after elevation
application never reads or stores password
Linux launcher never starts IDE as root without proven invoking user
risks.mitigation: retain and test the Linux fixed-function PolicyKit boundary; implement an equivalent minimal structured UAC helper for Windows so whole-app Administrator is not required
risks.verification: Linux and Windows desktop control plane plus IDE run unprivileged while only a bounded helper performs privileged TUN preparation; helper interface rejects arbitrary command execution

risks.title: sing-box schema or supply-chain drift breaks networking
risks.failure_mode: future sing-box release changes schema/behavior or a privileged artifact loses provenance
risks.effect: startup failure, changed routing semantics or privileged dependency compromise
risks.cause: external privileged dependency
controls: mandatory official SHA-256 for Agent Tunnel
real sing-box config check in CI
risks.mitigation: add explicit compatibility contract before dependency upgrades plus release SBOM/provenance/signing
risks.verification: dependency upgrade PR passes schema/runtime matrix and release provenance policy

risks.title: Local control plane can be exposed beyond loopback by configuration
risks.failure_mode: listen address is changed from loopback to a LAN/public interface
risks.effect: remote callers can reach privileged actions
risks.cause: historically listen address was configurable without a hard isolation invariant
controls: loopback-only validation for control plane and local proxy
risks.mitigation: normal mode is permanently loopback-only; future remote mode requires separate authenticated design
risks.verification: config tests reject wildcard/non-loopback addresses and observability API stays authenticated loopback-only

risks.title: Emergency hosts override becomes stale
risks.failure_mode: temporary Google IP remains pinned after topology/backend changes
risks.effect: future connectivity/TLS failures unrelated to active proxy mode
risks.cause: hosts entries have no TTL and survive process restart
risks.mitigation: record ownership/expiry metadata and warn or auto-remove stale override at startup
risks.verification: restart/time-shift tests prove expired override is detected and safely removed

risks.title: Power loss or external kill leaves orphan network state
risks.failure_mode: SIGKILL, kernel crash or power loss prevents graceful sing-box cleanup
risks.effect: stale TUN or policy routing state at next launch
risks.cause: process cleanup cannot run after non-cooperative termination
controls: real SIGKILL recovery fixture preserves unrelated routing state
risks.mitigation: extend forced termination coverage across every journal phase and add stronger orphan-helper ownership before process termination
risks.verification: forced termination leaves recoverable evidence; next launch repairs only owned state and returns to clean evidence

risks.title: Backend/account eligibility failure is misclassified as transport failure
risks.failure_mode: FAILED_PRECONDITION/PERMISSION_DENIED is treated as a routing problem
risks.effect: user repeatedly escalates networking changes that cannot fix server-side eligibility
risks.cause: UI-level agent error is generic and multiple root causes share the same message
risks.mitigation: make backend-vs-transport classification first-class and stop escalation on authoritative server rejection
risks.verification: fixture logs for geo/account, quota, MCP, auth and 5xx produce deterministic next actions

risks.title: Managed sing-box update removes Linux file capabilities
risks.failure_mode: managed binary is replaced during update and loses required capability xattrs
risks.effect: Agent Tunnel fails to start until capabilities are restored
risks.cause: file capabilities belong to the replaced inode
controls: ordinary-user readiness detects missing capabilities on every explicit Agent Tunnel start
one-shot fixed-function PolicyKit helper automatically reapplies exact required capabilities
helper revalidates expected path, ownership and SHA-256 around setcap
risks.mitigation: add an ordinary-user upgrade fixture across supported distro families proving replacement-induced xattr loss is automatically detected and repaired through PolicyKit before Tunnel startup
risks.verification: upgrade fixture replaces managed binary, removes capabilities, then proves one OS authorization restores the exact capability set and tunnel starts without whole-app elevation
plan_refs: P1 automatic Linux capability repair and upgrade fixture

risks.title: TUN policy conflicts with Docker, VM or network-manager routes
risks.failure_mode: auto_route/strict policy overlaps another routing manager or custom policy table
risks.effect: unrelated workloads lose connectivity or tunnel startup fails
risks.cause: desktop hosts have heterogeneous policy routing, VPNs, containers and virtual interfaces
controls: Linux strict capture proven in isolated dual-egress runtime
risks.mitigation: expand conflict runtime matrix across Docker/Podman, VM managers, NetworkManager/systemd-networkd and concurrent VPNs
risks.verification: runtime matrix preserves unrelated connectivity and refuses ambiguous ownership before mutation

risks.title: Mixed proxy port health masks a broken TUN or route
risks.failure_mode: local proxy accepts connections while TUN/process routing/DNS is unhealthy
risks.effect: UI reports success even though agent execution uses wrong path
risks.cause: single-dimensional reachability is insufficient evidence
controls: bounded external-egress cache with freshness metadata
risks.mitigation: add route, DNS v4/v6, selected-egress, agent-process and backend dimensions plus transient lifecycle states and cancellable operation IDs
risks.verification: fault injection independently breaks each dimension and API/UI reports partial/degraded/verified accurately

risks.title: Selected egress invariant is not continuously verified on the real host
risks.failure_mode: configuration looks correct but actual process ownership, chosen outbound or external egress differs
risks.effect: geo-sensitive backend sees wrong network despite green local status
risks.cause: static config cannot prove kernel/runtime egress and helper topology changes
controls: bounded egress TTL and lifecycle invalidation
risks.mitigation: add full Windows end-to-end proof and independent IPv4/IPv6 plus UDP/QUIC assurance
risks.verification: every active agent PID has exact socket ownership, vpn-direct evidence and fresh external egress evidence; mismatch blocks verified state

risks.title: Shutdown timeout or SIGKILL prevents deterministic cleanup
risks.failure_mode: sing-box ignores SIGTERM and forced termination happens before cleanup
risks.effect: network state can remain until next recovery
risks.cause: bounded shutdown must eventually force-kill a stuck helper
controls: forced timeout intentionally leaves recovery journal open
risks.mitigation: extend forced-timeout/restart fixture across every journal boundary
risks.verification: forced-timeout tests prove next launch repairs owned residual state while unrelated state survives

risks.title: main branch is not protected by required CI checks
risks.failure_mode: a direct push can land without successful test/risk gates
risks.effect: networking regressions can reach main despite strong CI definitions
risks.cause: repository branch protection is currently disabled
controls: riskcheck and privileged runtime are defined in CI
native Windows and Linux build/runtime jobs exist
risks.mitigation: enable main branch protection/ruleset and require test, linux-tun-runtime, windows-unit, riskcheck, race and platform builds
risks.verification: GitHub rules reject a merge/push path lacking required successful checks

risks.title: Linux runtime portability is under-tested outside Ubuntu amd64
risks.failure_mode: ARM64 or another distro differs in capabilities, resolver or routing behavior
risks.effect: build succeeds but Agent Tunnel fails at runtime
risks.cause: privileged CI currently runs only Ubuntu amd64
risks.mitigation: add Debian/Fedora-family runtime matrix and native/virtual ARM64 privileged runner
risks.verification: same TUN lifecycle, recovery, privilege bootstrap and dual-egress assertions pass on each supported target
plan_refs: P4 Linux ARM64 and distro matrix

risks.title: Diagnostics can disclose tokens, IPs or user paths
risks.failure_mode: support bundle contains sensitive authentication/network/local-path information
risks.effect: credential or privacy exposure when report is shared
risks.cause: logs and assurance evidence originate from multiple components with inconsistent formats
controls: Agent Doctor redacts bearer/OAuth token values
sing-box API secret is not returned by control plane
Windows POSIX FileMode is not treated as ACL proof
risks.mitigation: central redaction pipeline plus native Windows security-descriptor verification for sensitive files
risks.verification: synthetic secret/path/IP corpus produces zero prohibited cleartext matches and Windows ACL fixture proves unintended principals cannot read secrets

risks.title: Static Antigravity backend endpoint list drifts
risks.failure_mode: Google adds or changes agent/model backend hostname and it is absent from current policy
risks.effect: new agent flow bypasses intended routing or fails
risks.cause: backend topology evolves independently
controls: PID/socket attestation can expose new helper connection
risks.mitigation: learn backend hostnames from command line, SNI and logs, then require review before persisting policy
risks.verification: new-host fixture demonstrates unknown endpoint is surfaced and routed only after reviewed policy

risks.title: Settings/UI contract drifts from tunnel orchestration
risks.failure_mode: visible setting is persisted but ignored by StartAgentTunnel or another action
risks.effect: operator believes safety/routing option is active when runtime uses defaults
risks.cause: settings, web UI and orchestration evolve independently
risks.mitigation: add API-to-runtime contract tests for every exposed setting and canonical documentation consistency tests
risks.verification: each UI/config field changes generated runtime config or is explicitly rejected/normalized; canonical docs cannot regress to stale routing/privilege semantics

risks.title: Local proxy port collision creates false-positive health
risks.failure_mode: another process listens on configured mixed port while managed sing-box is absent or failed
risks.effect: health appears valid and Antigravity can be launched through unintended local service
risks.cause: port reachability alone does not prove service identity
controls: SAFE and Agent Tunnel readiness use ownership evidence
risks.mitigation: add explicit foreign-listener negative fixture and cryptographic/launch-token ownership for orphan-helper operations
risks.verification: fake service occupies port; health/readiness fail and no unrelated PID is killed
plan_refs: P1 managed listener and orphan ownership

risks.title: Installer accepts release asset when digest evidence is absent
risks.failure_mode: privileged Agent Tunnel installer proceeds without usable official SHA-256 evidence
risks.effect: privileged binary authenticity is weaker than intended
risks.cause: historical MVP path was warning-only when digest metadata was absent
risks.mitigation: retain fail-closed verified installation path and provenance checks for every privileged reuse
risks.verification: unit tests reject missing digest evidence and modified installed binary

risks.title: Configuration writes are not uniformly atomic
risks.failure_mode: remaining direct-write path can be interrupted and leave partial state
risks.effect: settings/configuration can become ambiguous after crash or power loss
risks.cause: atomic helper is implemented but not every legacy write path migrated
controls: central atomicfile helper with fsync/write-through and previous-good
risks.mitigation: migrate remaining SAFE proxy/Antigravity settings/hosts metadata writes and add interruption fault injection; independently verify Windows ACLs
risks.verification: every persistent state file has old-or-new completeness and previous-good recovery; sensitive Windows files pass native ACL fixtures

risks.title: Stale-state recovery deletes an unrelated concurrent route or rule
risks.failure_mode: route/rule changed by another network manager during Agent Tunnel lifetime is misclassified as owned and removed
risks.effect: unrelated host connectivity or policy is damaged by recovery
risks.cause: before/after differencing can confuse concurrent mutations with Agent Tunnel mutations
controls: only wholly new route tables absent from baseline are otherwise flushed
only new rule priorities absent from baseline are otherwise deleted
SIGKILL recovery fixture preserves unrelated route/rule
risks.mitigation: expand concurrent-network-manager recovery fixtures across supported managers and platforms
risks.verification: inject unrelated route/rule changes while active, crash helper, recover, and prove unrelated changes survive

risks.title: Network-state journal is corrupted or semantically incomplete
risks.failure_mode: journal cannot be decoded or lacks enough evidence after interrupted write/version drift
risks.effect: automatic recovery cannot safely decide what it owns
risks.cause: recovery correctness depends on durable metadata across crashes and upgrades
controls: corruption fixtures prove no broad cleanup
risks.mitigation: complete explicit old-schema migration contract and fault-injection matrix for every journal phase
risks.verification: truncated/corrupted/old-schema journals never cause broad cleanup and produce deterministic recovery guidance

risks.title: Windows stale route cleanup lacks strong route ownership proof
risks.failure_mode: previous helper is gone but interface-scoped route residue cannot be safely mapped to owned route objects
risks.effect: Windows may require manual cleanup or remain degraded after abnormal termination
risks.cause: current Windows recovery avoids broad route deletion without stable interface LUID/table ownership
controls: automatic broad Windows route deletion disabled
risks.mitigation: bind recovery evidence to Windows interface LUID/route compartment and delete only exact owned route objects
risks.verification: forced-kill Windows integration test proves exact owned-route cleanup while unrelated routes survive
plan_refs: P1 Windows exact route ownership recovery
